question: How should one-shot scheduled publication atomically materialize one occurrence and retain a terminal skipped or fired record across retries and scheduler restarts?
scope: Atomic occurrence outcome, misfire and pending cancellation
Restore fencing of uncertain scheduled intent

authority_boundary.authority_source: Accepted coordination v1 implementation/deployment goal and trusted-host correction
authorized_scope: Implement and deploy milestone6 one-shot scheduling under existing local operator authority

evidence.summary: Milestone6 requires one-shot due scheduling, stable occurrence identity and audited misfires before later deadline/cancellation work. Existing PostgreSQL, store-owned attribution, explicit trusted-host operator scope and disposable test rules apply. The one-shot contract distinguishes publication grace, pending cancellation and restore uncertainty from running-work control.

evidence.summary: Create allocates one occurrence UUID. Tick holds shared restore generation then collection insertion lock then due schedule rows, creates the same UUID event/fanout via the existing publication rules, and updates terminal outcome within one transaction. Pool refusals roll back their savepoint and rotate pending intent; other store failures propagate. Cancel shares the collection lock. Restore marks pending schedules skipped before later ticks can execute. Publisher remains current store channel, matched to creator.

evidence.summary: Full make test-integration and make check passed; make test-lifecycle compared populated fired/pending/skipped/cancelled schedules through actual backup/restore. Real CLI daemon was observed ready, stopped before due and restarted after due; it emitted exactly the reserved event UUID once. Store tests cover concurrent ticks, injected terminal-update rollback, source retraction/deletion, exact retry/conflicting intent, topic subscription changes, blocked-pool rotation, cancel/fire race, explicit DST offsets and restore fencing. Final test-only change scoped the failure trigger to its occurrence and was re-run with -race.

assertions.text: Concurrent ticks serialize occurrence publication and terminal state; injected terminal-update failure rolls back the event and delivery. Exact creation retries preserve the occurrence UUID.
Use one-shot intent with explicit grace, retained terminal outcomes, same-operator attribution and restore fencing. Pool pressure preserves pending intent within grace; unexpected errors propagate.

alternatives.option: Commit scheduled event, fanout and occurrence outcome in one PostgreSQL transaction
Publish in one transaction then mark the schedule fired in another
Keep shell timers without retained occurrence identity

verification_criteria: Disposable full integration with race detector and static checks
Real scheduler readiness, restart and stable UUID delivery
Populated schedule backup/restore comparison and explicit restore fencing
reopening_conditions: Another schedule/event creator changes the lock order
Recurring calendars or hosted scheduling need a concrete caller contract
Measured queue contention exceeds bounded rotation requirements

Restore may have lost later effects; pending occurrences are skipped for review. Same-operator local scheduling does not add credentials or impersonate hosted agents.
